verdict_definitions.correct: Inspected primary evidence supports the bounded claim or metadata.
verdict_definitions.fault: A directly evidenced contradiction or false attribution; none established among the checked claims.
verdict_definitions.unresolved: Specific detail not freshly verified; not assumed false or inherited as true from the prior review.

summary.traceability_gap: CLQT v3 informs two frozen rubric bases but is not named in the audited manuscript/prior paper review.
interpretive_clarifications: E2A directional coverage differs from eleven-row or transport coverage.
Evidence locators and isolated rubric checks improve auditability; their bias-reduction efficacy here remains unmeasured.
PortBench settings do not validate local semantic categories, numeric tolerances or pilot size.
summary.scope_limit: A count of zero detected contradictions is not a universal bibliography or measurement-validity certification.

locators: B decision-time market context; B.2 correlation estimation

checked_claims.claim: Temperature 0 and maximum output 8192, with thinking enabled in the source study.
60-trading-day lookback, 252 annualization, equal-weight and long-only minimum-variance comparators.
Half-L1 distance is the complement of Eq.8 reference similarity for normalized long-only portfolios.
Information ablation removes supplied covariance information.

reference_checks.boundary: These are settings and diagnostics from a different task. They do not validate local sample size, tolerance, categorical semantic rubric, institutional numeric targets, or the model configuration. The manuscript already states thinking is off locally and avoids a replication claim.
reference_checks.clarification: ddof=1 was not established from the inspected HTML; retain it as a disclosed local estimator choice. The manuscript attributes only 60 observations and annualization to PortBench, so no contradiction was found.

manuscript_reference.text: Yuxuan Zhao, Sijia Chen, Ningxin Su (2026). PortBench: A Correlation-Aware, Full-Pipeline Benchmark for LLM-Driven Portfolio Management. arXiv:2605.27887. v6, 9 October 2026.

checked_claims.claim: Evidence grounding, rationale/action consistency, confidence, and coverage are distinct diagnostics.
Its coverage and NDR measure evidence-to-action reliability rather than realized returns.

reference_checks.boundary: Coverage here means the proportion committing to BUY/SELL, not the presence of eleven sector rows or mere successful completion. The local adaptation is conceptual, not an imported validated scale. Source scorer validation by four finance practitioners does not validate local AI coding.
reference_checks.clarification: Keep the arXiv citation; an EMNLP Findings comment alone does not verify a proceedings record.

manuscript_reference.text: Xiaoya Wang, Yutong Xu, Junjie Wang (2026). E2A-Bench: Benchmarking Evidence-to-Action Reliability in Financial Chart Reasoning. arXiv:2609.14302. v1, 13 September 2026.

checked_claims.claim: Self/family preference persists with objective rubric-based judgments; multiple judges can mitigate without eliminating it.

reference_checks.boundary: Granular or isolated review is not sufficient to eliminate self-preference. Exact-field evidence logging improves auditability, but its bias-reduction effect in this project is unmeasured. The manuscript states intent and explicitly disclaims unbiasedness/human validation.

manuscript_reference.text: José Pombal, Ricardo Rei, André F. T. Martins (2026). Self-Preference Bias in Rubric-Based Evaluation of Large Language Models. arXiv:2604.06996. v3, 3 August 2026.

reference_checks.title: CLQT: A Closed-Loop, Cost-Aware, Strategy-Consistent Benchmark for Diagnostic Evaluation of LLM Portfolio-Management Agents

checked_claims.claim: Mechanical signal/action direction and stated-analysis/allocation coherence are separate checks.
A held-out judge helps address bias but does not establish independence or eliminate self-preference.

reference_checks.boundary: Its human anchoring uses one blinded author, not an independent expert panel. It supplies motivation for process diagnostics; it does not validate this project's categories, thresholds, or institution-weight mapping.
reference_checks.traceability: Named in two frozen rubric bases but absent from both supplied manuscript and prior paper review. This is a documentation gap, not an incorrect existing citation or a requirement to add another study. A future manuscript may name it where this specific distinction is discussed.

checked_claims.claim: A more accurate shared algorithm can worsen aggregate outcomes under the paper's competitive selection model.

reference_checks.boundary: A conditional theoretical motivation; not evidence that current financial institutions herd or that this small allocation study measures welfare.

manuscript_reference.text: Jon Kleinberg, Manish Raghavan (2021). Algorithmic monoculture and social welfare. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 118(22), e2018340118.

checked_claims.claim: Foundation-model sharing has mixed homogenization results depending on adaptation methods.

reference_checks.boundary: Supports separating common-tool use from the degree of outcome homogenization; does not directly test institutional allocation prompts.

manuscript_reference.text: Rishi Bommasani, Kathleen A. Creel, Ananya Kumar, Dan Jurafsky, Percy Liang (2022). Picking on the Same Person: Does Algorithmic Monoculture lead to Outcome Homogenization? Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 35.

checked_claims.claim: AI ideas can improve evaluated short-story quality while making the set of stories more similar.

reference_checks.boundary: Creative-writing evidence motivates a quality/diversity distinction, not financial-return or institutional-herding estimates. Direct DOI open was 403 and PMC open was a browser challenge; UCL repository metadata/abstract and publisher-indexed content were available.

manuscript_reference.text: Anil R. Doshi, Oliver P. Hauser (2024). Generative AI enhances individual creativity but reduces the collective diversity of novel content. Science Advances, 10, eadn5290.

checked_claims.claim: The study compares domain-information conditions within a common portfolio allocation task.

manuscript_reference.text: Lars Hornuf, David J. Streich, Niklas Töllich (2025). Making GenAI Smarter: Evidence from a Portfolio Allocation Experiment. CESifo Working Paper No. 11862.

reference_checks.boundary: The paper explicitly uses official release dates for macro memories and prior-day news. It does not establish that this project's selected seven facts or GDP substitution are uniquely optimal.

reference_checks.boundary: Motivates studying provision procedures. It does not isolate a pure timing, memory or psychological anchoring effect in this project; manuscript block13 correctly declares combined exposure/draft/history differences.

reference_checks.boundary: This establishes a comparative-evaluation bias risk, not the efficacy of the project's isolated-field coding or a guarantee that its coding has no bias.

reference_checks.boundary: Official release supports the manuscript's potential-risk wording. Report landing-page open timed out; full report not re-read. This is a policy motivation, not observed causal institutional homogenization.

errors.reason: Official identities/versions and central claims agree. No concrete contradiction found; two original-text details remain unverified, and access failures are recorded.

consistency.reason: Three read local inputs have identical before/after hashes. Version pins and local-adaptation disclaimers agree with primary sources. CLQT protocol-to-manuscript traceability and coverage terminology merit bounded clarification.

paper_topic.reason: The bridge remains institution evidence interpretation and its connection to observable allocation under common AI. It does not expand into trading-performance ranking, institution herding measurement or evaluator-validation claims.

changes.note: Only this new report is written; no original source, manuscript, rubric, prompt, frozen code, or live-run artifact is changed.
